title: Benchmark: add streaming chat end-to-end runner (TTFT/TPOT + phase breakdowns)
author: Rina Kobayashi
body:
Title: Benchmark: add streaming chat end-to-end runner (TTFT/TPOT + phase breakdowns)

Context
We need a first-class end-to-end benchmark scenario for hosted-style streaming chat to quantify quantized (FP8/INT8) runtime changes under realistic traffic shapes. This PR adds a new runner that measures TTFT/TPOT and produces a per-phase breakdown (client-side request overhead, prefill, decode, stream flush) with metadata needed for the sprint report and perf-canary ingestion.

This is specifically scoped to ENG-24811 as part of the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint.

What’s in this PR
- New benchmark scenario: `streaming_chat_e2e` (streaming responses) driven by a prompt/workload spec.
- Captures and reports:
  - TTFT (time-to-first-token)
  - TPOT (time-per-output-token), computed over streamed tokens (excluding first token by default)
  - Tokens/sec (decode throughput proxy)
  - Phase timing breakdown: connect+TLS, request serialization, server wait (until first token), streaming loop, finalization
- Produces structured JSON results with stable field names and tags (model, quant_mode, gpu_sku, runtime_commit, workload_preset, region) so the report generator and dashboards can consume it.
- Adds workload knobs needed for streaming realism:
  - concurrency / max_in_flight
  - output token target (max_tokens)
  - server-side streaming cadence (if supported by endpoint)
  - client chunk aggregation threshold (to avoid per-byte overhead skew)
- Includes deterministic warmup and a latency-sample windowing approach to avoid counting startup jitters.

Design notes / methodology choices
- TTFT definition: wall-clock from request start (after connection established if reusing keepalive; included in metadata) to first decoded token event in the stream. We record both `ttft_ms` and `ttft_ms_including_connect` for transparency.
- TPOT definition: average inter-token delta over tokens 2..N in the stream (configurable). We also emit `tpot_p50_ms`, `tpot_p95_ms` across samples (per-request token deltas aggregated) to help tail analysis.
- Phase attribution: the runner timestamps key events (request_start, headers_sent, first_token, token_i, stream_end). This is not a replacement for server-side tracing; it’s a consistent end-to-end signal that correlates with scheduler changes.
- Streaming parser: supports SSE and chunked JSON; endpoint selection is config-driven. For Redwood-hosted endpoints we default to SSE.
- Guardrails: the runner validates that token count increases monotonically and that stream termination is well-formed; failed streams are recorded as errors with `error_type` rather than silently dropped.

Files / major changes
- `benchmarks/scenarios/streaming_chat_e2e.py`: new scenario runner + token event loop
- `benchmarks/metrics/streaming.py`: TTFT/TPOT calculators + token delta aggregation
- `benchmarks/results/schema.py`: adds `phase_timings_ms` fields and standard tag keys for streaming runs
- `benchmarks/config/schema.yaml`: adds `streaming_chat_e2e` scenario config
- `benchmarks/config/examples/streaming_chat_e2e.sample.yaml`: example config (single model, 2 concurrencies)
- `docs/scenarios.md`: scenario documentation + metric definitions
- `tests/test_streaming_metrics.py`: unit tests for TTFT/TPOT and edge cases (single-token output, dropped chunk)

Example output (abridged)
{
  "scenario": "streaming_chat_e2e",
  "workload": "qwen2.5-chat/streaming/p50",
  "metrics": {
    "ttft_ms_p50": 182.4,
    "ttft_ms_p95": 291.8,
    "tpot_ms_mean": 22.7,
    "tpot_ms_p95": 35.1,
    "output_tokens_mean": 256.3
  },
  "phase_timings_ms": {
    "connect": 0.0,
    "request_write": 4.3,
    "server_wait_first_token": 176.9,
    "streaming_loop": 5812.0,
    "finalize": 3.1
  },
  "tags": {
    "quant_mode": "fp8",
    "gpu_sku": "H100",
    "runtime_commit": "6d3c2f1",
    "region": "perf-lab-usw2"
  }
}

How to run
- Sample config:
  - `python -m benchmark_lab run --config benchmarks/config/examples/streaming_chat_e2e.sample.yaml`
- Typical sprint command (pinned runtime + tags):
  - `python -m benchmark_lab run --config <cfg> --tag runtime_commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) --tag quant_mode=fp8`

Open questions (follow-ups, not in this PR)
- Whether to treat keepalive reuse as the default for TTFT reporting in the sprint report (we record both; report can choose).
- Whether to emit per-token deltas as a separate artifact for deep dive (we currently aggregate; raw token timing is large). Can add behind a flag.

Checklist
- [x] Adds scenario docs
- [x] Unit tests for TTFT/TPOT edge cases
- [x] Results schema version bump + backward compatibility note
- [x] Verified against staging endpoint with SSE streaming

Linked work
- Linear: ENG-24811
- Related PRs: #412 (config schema + validation), #414 (workload presets/matrix generator)

Commits
1. `c1a4c0e` add streaming chat scenario skeleton + config wiring
2. `a39f7d2` implement SSE parser + token event loop with timestamps
3. `9b2f0a1` add TTFT/TPOT metric calculators + aggregation
4. `4d8b6bb` results schema: phase timings + tags
5. `e0c8a11` docs and sample config
6. `7fb1f2e` tests: streaming metrics edge cases

Review conversation
- Noah Patel (review): Can we separate connect time from server wait time? Otherwise TTFT will jump around based on keepalive reuse.
  - Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `ttft_ms` (excluding connect when keepalive reused) and `ttft_ms_including_connect`, plus `phase_timings_ms.connect`. Docs updated.
- Marcus Reed (review): TPOT mean is sensitive to first token; should exclude token 1 by default and report p95.
  - Rina: Done. Default excludes first token; emits `tpot_ms_mean`, `tpot_ms_p50`, `tpot_ms_p95` based on per-request token deltas.
- Allison Grant (review): Please align tag keys with dashboard conventions (gpu_sku, quant_mode, runtime_commit, model_family).
  - Rina: Updated tag normalization and docs. Added `model_family` derivation when the config includes `model_id`.
- Claire Dubois (review): Warmup should not be mixed with measured samples; also document retry/error behavior.
  - Rina: Warmup now runs as a separate phase; measured samples start after warmup completes. Added error recording semantics and a max-retry cap.

CI history
- 2025-10-08: integration failed due to flaky mock server timing; fixed by using a deterministic event scheduler and removing sleep-based assertions.

Merge
Squash merged by Rina Kobayashi into `main` on 2025-10-11.

Release note
Adds a new `streaming_chat_e2e` benchmark scenario producing TTFT/TPOT and phase timing breakdowns for end-to-end streaming chat performance tracking.
